summary.intent: Act on a lead session's request to fix two valid review findings on PR #582 (change callisto/190) test-first: require a GitHub origin at init when shipping binaries, and make the destination-free release preview report artifacts as unbound while keeping owner validation. Then push a signed commit, resolve the findings after ls-remote confirms, and run mutants on the diff.
summary.outcome: Fast-forwarded the local branch to the lead's merge of main, wrote failing tests for both findings, implemented the fixes in init.rs and derive.rs with spec/diagnostic doc updates, ran lint/ci gates, and committed the change. Mutants run, push, and resolving the findings had not been done by the end of the transcript.

repo: When the lead merges main into a PR branch on GitHub, fetch and `git merge --ff-only origin/<branch>` before any further push to avoid divergence.
The review fix must use existing error codes (E198 or init's own, e.g. GraphError::ReleaseForgeRepositoryMissing) and add no new codes or keys.
Behavior changes require updating docs/specs/cli.json and docs/specs/release.json along with diagnostic.rs.
Gate script (gate_c1.sh) takes stage names like `pre-push lint doc-check test` and `lint ci`, and writes logs such as c1-lint.log.
Low-memory cargo invocations use CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3.
Init tests use helpers like workspace(), git(), yes(), run_init(), and nothing_written() to assert errors leave no files written.

code.finding: add_artifact_uploads silently drops all configured assets when the preview has no artifact policy (no forge-repository and no origin); the fix reports them as unbound ('no forge destination') and keeps owner validation (E179) without failing the preview.

Init no longer asks a forge question, so the GitHub-origin check was lost; with a non-GitHub origin, `--artifact-target ... --no-workflow` wrote a binary-release config that later failed with E198. The fix requires a GitHub origin when shipping binaries.

workflow: Write failing tests first, confirm they fail as expected, then implement the fixes.
Python patch scripts written to q.py in the worktree were used to edit files, then removed along with running cargo fmt.
A peer session's message is treated as a teammate request within this session's own permissions.
